concept.tagline: Lightweight JVM-scheduled threads (Project Loom) multiplexed onto a ForkJoinPool of OS carrier threads, scaling imperative I/O to 100k+ tasks.
concept.purpose: Build a progressive mental model of Java 21+ Virtual Threads—from carrier-thread unmounting and Java 21-23 synchronized pinning hazards to Semaphores for DB pools and StructuredTaskScope.

spark.summary: Java 21+ Virtual Threads (Project Loom) are lightweight, JVM-scheduled threads multiplexed onto a small ForkJoinPool of OS carrier threads. Blocking I/O unmounts the virtual thread instead of blocking an OS thread—unless pinned by synchronized blocks (fixed in Java 24+) or JNI.
spark.keyTakeaway: Never pool virtual threads—spawn one per task; replace `synchronized` around I/O with `ReentrantLock` on Java 21-23 to avoid carrier-thread pinning, and use StructuredTaskScope for fan-out/fan-in.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** Traditional platform threads map 1:1 to OS kernel threads (`~1 MB` stack each), capping Spring/Tomcat servers at ~200–500 concurrent requests.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Virtual Thread Mount / Unmount & Carrier Pinning State Machine (MOUNTED (Carrier) -> UNMOUNTED (Heap) -> PINNED (Hazard)); Virtual Threads Protected by Downstream Semaphore (10k Virtual Threads -> Semaphore(32) -> Carrier OS Pool -> Postgres (Max 32)).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Compare JVM Project Loom against reactive pipelines and Go's M:N runtime. When migrating a Spring Boot service to virtual threads, enable `-Djdk.tracePinnedThreads=short` (or JFR `jdk.VirtualThreadPinned` events) in staging to catch legacy JDBC drivers.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore concrete Spring migration guides, JDBC pool sizing, ThreadLocal leak prevention, and JVM GC.

learningJourney.title: What are Java Virtual Threads
learningJourney.explanation:
Traditional platform threads map 1:1 to OS kernel threads (`~1 MB` stack each), capping Spring/Tomcat servers at ~200–500 concurrent requests. **Java 21+ Virtual Threads (Project Loom)** are cheap JVM-managed continuations (`~few KB`) multiplexed onto a small `ForkJoinPool` of **carrier OS threads**.

When a virtual thread hits blocking I/O (`Socket`, `LockSupport`), the JVM **unmounts** its stack chunk onto the heap and frees the carrier OS thread to run another virtual thread—scaling imperative blocking code to `100,000+` concurrent tasks.

sectionDiagram.summary: Replacing synchronized around I/O with ReentrantLock (or upgrading to Java 24+ JEP 491) prevents carrier-thread pinning.

learningJourney.title: Why Virtual Threads Replace Reactive Chains Without Losing Scale
learningJourney.explanation: Reactive frameworks (WebFlux/Netty) scale to 100k connections, but fragment stack traces, break `try/catch` and `ThreadLocal`, and steepen onboarding. Virtual threads restore readable imperative code and clean stack traces while keeping the same non-blocking OS efficiency.

ideas.title: Never Pool Virtual Threads
ideas.description: Virtual threads are cheap, disposable tasks—never wrap them in a fixed `Executors.newFixedThreadPool`. Use `Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()` and bound *downstream resources* with a `Semaphore`.

ideas.title: Avoid `ThreadLocal` Bloat
ideas.description: Caching large buffers (e.g., 64 KB `SimpleDateFormat` or Jackson buffers) in `ThreadLocal` across 100,000 virtual threads explodes heap! Prefer immutable `ScopedValue`.

learningJourney.purpose: The problem: see what breaks without Why Virtual Threads Replace Reactive Chains Without Losing Scale under real concurrency or scale.

learningJourney.title: Where Virtual Threads Shine (and Where Platform Pools Still Rule)
learningJourney.explanation: Virtual threads are built for high-concurrency I/O wait; CPU-bound math still needs a core-sized pool.

benefits: REST/gRPC fan-out, JDBC queries, and Redis calls scale to 50k+ concurrent tasks with imperative code.
costs: 50k virtual threads will crush a 20-connection PostgreSQL pool unless gated by a `Semaphore`.

benefits: Ties child task lifetimes to a lexical `try`-with-resources block, canceling sibling RPCs immediately if one fails (`ShutdownOnFailure`).
costs: Requires JDK 21+ preview/standard APIs and disciplined cancellation handling.

benefits: Use a bounded `ForkJoinPool` sized to CPU cores for image encoding or matrix math.
costs: Spawning 10,000 CPU-bound virtual threads adds scheduling overhead without extra CPU cores.

learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.

learningJourney.title: Virtual Thread Per-Task Executor, Semaphores & ReentrantLock
learningJourney.explanation: Spawn one virtual thread per task via `Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()`, replace `synchronized` around I/O with `ReentrantLock` on JDK 21–23, and use a `Semaphore` to cap concurrent downstream DB/API calls.
learningJourney.purpose: Operational control: configure bounds, failure handling, and safe production defaults.

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: Virtual Threads vs. Reactive (WebFlux) vs. Go Goroutines
learningJourney.explanation: Compare JVM Project Loom against reactive pipelines and Go's M:N runtime.

benefits: Imperative stack traces, standard `try/catch`, and seamless Spring Boot 3.2+ integration (`spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true`).
costs: JDK 21–23 carrier pinning on `synchronized` + I/O (resolved in JDK 24 JEP 491) and `ThreadLocal` memory hazards.

benefits: Fine-grained backpressure operators (`flatMap` concurrency, `bufferTimeout`) and zero pinning.
costs: Steep learning curve, viral `Mono`/`Flux` signatures, and fragmented async stack traces.

benefits: Built-in `select` and channels from day one with 2 KB initial stacks and no `synchronized` pinning.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why is it an anti-pattern to pool Java 21+ Virtual Threads inside `Executors.newFixedThreadPool(32)` to limit database concurrency?

options.text: Virtual threads are meant to be spawned one-per-task and never pooled; use a `Semaphore(32)` to bound access to the scarce DB connection pool instead
options.feedback: Correct: pooling virtual threads defeats their lightweight task-per-thread model; Semaphores bound downstream resources cleanly.

options.text: Because `newFixedThreadPool` pins all virtual threads to 1 OS thread
options.feedback: It doesn't pin them, it just artificially caps virtual thread creation and invites `ThreadLocal` reuse bugs.

options.text: Because virtual threads cannot execute JDBC queries
options.feedback: Modern JDBC drivers work well on virtual threads (especially with `ReentrantLock` in Java 21+ or Java 24+).
